name: Heca
goal:
MANDATORY: read AGENTS.md in full.
Consolidare Heca come workspace compositor nativo, keyboard-first e pluggable, completando piattaforma terminale, architettura chrome/plugin, libreria grid-ui, integrazione Neovim GUI e rifiniture app/chrome.
The gates before any code
- §0 pre-flight, three written answers, per thing touched: which existing widget does this → if none, which planner task covers it (quote the id) → if neither, it is a proposal, not a commit.
- §0b widget vs component: if it can be built inside heca-grid-ui, it belongs there. A component only leaves the library because it binds an app concept.
- §0c the event system is DOM-shaped — capture → target → bubble, keys do bubble, a widget never hit-tests and never forwards, nothing focused means nothing delivered, and a cursor inside a container is not focus. Reach for a handler before an intent, a policy arm or a registry.
- ⭐⭐ Rule Zero: write the line a plugin author would type. A registry, an id or a crate-private type means the API is missing. HintTargetRegistry, HintTargets, HintTargetId, Base::hint_target, named_press are gone and must not come back.
description: Compositore di workspace GPU-native per sviluppatori, ispirato al layout a colonne scrollabili di Niri, che unifica terminali, editor e strumenti in una singola finestra accelerata via GPU. Think tmux meets Niri meets Neovide: terminali, editor e futuri container/plugin convivono nello stesso frame con animazioni fluide, testo nitido e chrome renderizzato via GPU.

projectGuidelines.content:
- do not fix at call site. Always try to fix at library (widget/ component) side.
- use css like syntax for laying down components: Flex, Grid, Surface etc...
- prefer composition and reusability. DO NOT HARDCODE anything.

## Worktree Lifecycle (Antonio, 2026-10-27)

- From the next coding activity, start every new task in its own new worktree and branch from the latest synchronized main. Name its folder heca-feat-[num]. Do not reuse another task's worktree or edit application code/assets directly in main.
- Finish implementation and verification, mark the task DONE with durable completion evidence, and commit/push the canonical planner updates on main before opening the code PR toward main. After the merge is verified, the same agent removes its worktree, folder and merged branch. Do not leave cleanup or an unlanded task to Antonio or another agent.
- Verify cleanliness, merged content and active use before removing anything. Preserve all other agents' work and shared dirty changes.
- Leave the current worktrees as they are; do not retroactively rename or remove them to enforce the new naming rule.
- The canonical shared planner remains /Users/antonio/projects/heca/.planner; use planner tools there rather than independent worktree copies. Commit and push its updates from main so every developer/agent receives the same task, phase, feature and decision state by pull. Never replace it with a stale worktree planner or graphify copy.

acceptedDecisions.title: Public component authoring APIs expose ordinary constructors and children, without Box or casts
acceptedDecisions.decision: Public APIs used to author app, native-extension and described-plugin component trees must use ordinary component constructors, typed builders and child composition. They must not expose Box<dyn Component> as an authoring parameter or return value, require Box::new, trait-object casts, or explicit storage/type-erasure conversions merely to compose components. Allocation and type erasure are internal framework responsibilities. Public APIs and examples must let authors compose concrete components directly.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio explicitly confirmed on 2026-10-24 that Box and casts must be removed from public APIs. This generalizes the existing Pane-specific authoring constraint without changing the decision that pane content is open component composition.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes:
Approved 2026-10-25: apply this ordinary constructor/fluent composition contract to ALL supported public native widgets/components, factories and return boundaries, not Terminal alone. Heterogeneous children may chain .child(a).child(b); shared child/metadata mechanisms and internal allocation are reused. Plugin identity handles remain acceptable; sandbox SDK descriptions and native live components expose equivalent capabilities without sharing runtime objects.
Centralized implementation: P067(F003)/T517 (moved intact from P052) fixes generic parts/templates first; P067/T398 then owns registry/model migration, public constructors including standalone Terminal::new("shell"), native binding and the exhaustive public-authoring acceptance. No caller boxing/casts/manual conversions or private host contexts.
P094 retains terminal-header composition (T450), managed creation/lifecycle/restore consuming that API (T452), float/input audits (T453/T455), second-content proof (T454) and picker convergence (T457). Do not make T398 depend back on T452. P106(F011)/T550 now owns real multi-document tabs and retains its T452 task prerequisite; do not block tabs on closure of all P094.
P052 retains T118/T122/T350 closeouts without duplicating the global API. T253/T305 remain deferred/on-demand; T251/T474/T520 and other completed foundations stay done. T360 review, F012 integration and P022 actual WASM loading/startup parity retain their owners. One canonical Provider/region reference is docs/widgets.md; other guides link there. Planner operations always use /Users/antonio/projects/heca/.planner. Task dependencies, task descriptions and the P067/P094 handoffs record the operational resume sequence; planning changes do not authorize implementation/task-start or claim runtime verification.

acceptedDecisions.title: Terminal engine is wezterm-term over portable-pty, not alacritty_terminal or vte
acceptedDecisions.decision: heca's terminal stack is wezterm-term plus wezterm-surface (both pinned to wezterm git rev 891bed31b75f7a71b78e8f42ad07ae89bf99a7de) for emulation, and portable-pty 0.9.0 for the PTY. Verified in heca-core/Cargo.toml lines 14, 19, 20. It is NOT alacritty_terminal and NOT vte. The old planning files (the project file at line 63 "alacritty_terminal over Kitty/Ghostty", the requirements file entry PANE-01 and the stack research file at lines 5-27, all now a historical archive) said alacritty_terminal; they were out of date.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The code moved from alacritty_terminal to wezterm-term, and the reason for the change was never written down anywhere in the repo, so none is recorded here. The pinned rev matters: at 891bed31 wezterm-term has AlertHandler/NotificationHandler (bells) and get_title() (OSC 0/2) but no general OSC-dispatch callback, which is why heca scans OSC 133/7 itself before advance_bytes (see the pane runtime state decision on P054(F006)).
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Two docs still state the wrong engine: AGENTS.md:1162 (stack table says alacritty_terminal) and README.md:78 (says vte). Fix both in the T561 doc rewrite. Ask Antonio if he wants the original reason for the switch added.

acceptedDecisions.title: Architecture principle: all state that fires an action or updates content flows through AppState, so plugins can see it
acceptedDecisions.decision: Source: the "Architecture principles (apply to every task)" section of the old backlog file (now a historical archive). Verbatim rule: all state that fires an action or updates content MUST flow through AppState / the reactive chrome store, never be local-only. Any behavior that changes app state or triggers an action has to be dispatched through AppState (mirrored into the reactive store, emitted on the ChromeEvent bus, exposed via the host API) so that plugins and other components can listen and react (for example render their own custom widget). Make it signal-aware: store the value in a Signal, guard the setter (emit only on a real change), and add a ChromeEvent plus a StateView selector. Reference implementations: the KeyHint pending-pick description (InputMode::pending_pick() -> WorkspacesContainerState.pending_pick signal -> ChromeEvent::PendingPickChanged -> host.pending_pick()) and the pane custom name (PaneCustomNameChanged / host.pane_custom_name). Anti-pattern: computing a value only for an internal render path (the way the pick prompt used to live only in status_mode_parts). "If a plugin can't observe it, it's not done."
acceptedDecisions.rationale: AGENTS.md Rule Zero is the nearest text and does not state this rule. It is stated nowhere else now that the old backlog file is only a historical archive. Open work that applies it: P035(F003)/T506 and P085(F003)/T357.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Add one paragraph under Rule Zero in AGENTS.md during the T561 doc rewrite. Related: the pane runtime state decision on P054(F006) (one mutation point, signals plus event bus). Related idea I001 (status_note is the anti-pattern: a host-private string on AppState).

acceptedDecisions.title: The syntax: every widget and component is declarative and nested — Component::new().props(..).child(Grid/Flex::new().child([a, b]).template(..))
acceptedDecisions.decision: Every widget and component in heca (library, app, plugins) is written in one declarative, nested expression, Flutter/SwiftUI-shaped with DOM-shaped events: `Component::new().prop_a(..).child(Grid::new().template_row("auto 1fr").child([header, body])).on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(Intent::new("an_action")))`. Never: find a child by position (children[0]), write a style/bound/position by hand, rebuild a widget to change one property, or put a number in the code. If something cannot be written in this shape, the library is missing a builder — propose it (RULE ZERO), never work around it.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio, 2026-11-18, after a review showed much of the code (the command palette, the terminal component, ~20 library widgets) built imperatively: "la sintassi deve essere: Component::new().props(...).child(Flex.new().child([Comp1, comp2]).template....) … Metti in rilievo quella sintassi dove serve altrimenti nessuno la segue." The examples already existed (docs/layout.md:35, docs/widgets.md:2342) but were not where every reader starts.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: The block is written at the top of CLAUDE.md (loaded in every session), at the start of AGENTS.md § 0 and at the top of docs/widgets.md (branch docs/declarative-syntax, worktree heca-feat-syntax). For Button/IconButton `.on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(..))` works fully only after P087(F011)/T565 (one click path). A declarative child list bound to data (ForEach-like) is not in the library yet; Keyed / on_props / reconcile_keyed are the low-level mechanisms underneath.

acceptedDecisions.title: heca's public surface used by heca-pro stays compatible; heca-pro follows the same declarative syntax
acceptedDecisions.decision: The surface F012 "Ready for heca-pro" delivered (heca as a library and its extension entry point, server/client split and wire protocol, sessions, the RPC line format, extension services, the widgets) stays API-compatible: no silent breaking change — add the new form beside the old, mark the old deprecated, and agree the removal with Antonio and heca-pro. heca-pro itself follows the same declarative syntax (decision 05a2ed0c) and states the same rule in its own AGENTS.md.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio, 2026-11-18: "La feature ready for heca pro deve mantenere la compatibilità delle api. Heca pro stesso dovrà aderire alla sintassi e riportare nel suo agent.md la stessa regola sulla sintassi del codice."

acceptedDecisions.title: Release installers are built with cargo-packager; zips by a workflow step
acceptedDecisions.decision: heca's release installers (.dmg/.app on macOS, .deb + AppImage on Linux, .msi on Windows) are produced by cargo-packager (crabnebula-dev). The zip / tar.gz archives are made by a step of the release workflow. cargo-dist was not chosen.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio approved 2026-11-18. cargo-packager covers every installer asked for with one tool and one config (and also emits a pacman PKGBUILD, reusable for AUR, idea I025). cargo-dist covers zips and msi but has no dmg (future), no deb and no AppImage (axodotdev cargo-dist book, installers page).
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Workflow and configuration in P110(F010)/T566. Whether each format must be built on its own OS is to be verified in the v0.1.0-rc1 test release.

acceptedDecisions.title: THE EVENTS: one way to listen, everywhere — on("name", |ev| …)
acceptedDecisions.decision: Every listener in heca — heca's own components and providers, an extension (native, including its server services) and a plugin (WASM included) — subscribes to a state change with the same line: `on("dotted.name", …)`, plus `"*"` for every event. Names are dotted, `<subject>.<what>.changed` style (pane.cwd.changed, chrome.container.focus.changed, session.changed). One event per subject when the changes are rare and a listener wants them together; it carries a `kind` field naming what happened (session.changed: created | renamed | terminated | restarted | deleted) and the data a listener needs, so it does not have to read state back. Never a signal, a polling loop, a dedicated trait method or a per-consumer callback in its place. Each event is emitted from ONE mutation point, and the same event reaches the scripts' stream (`heca rpc --events`). Handler shape follows the place it is declared: a window component `cx.on(name, |ev| …)`; a server service `service.on(name, |service, cx, ev| …)`, handed the service itself like the service's actions and policies.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio, 2026-11-19: "deve essere chiaro che anche nei plugins sarà questa la sintassi. È evidenziato?" The contract already existed — P054(F006) decision "Pane runtime state … (locked 2026-06-18)", section 0.1: a typed event bus so plugins and providers react with app.on(name, handler), because plugins cannot subscribe to internal signals — but it was written only in that decision and deep in docs/chrome-and-ui.md (244, 287, 780, 1182, 1236), so an agent designing the server-side session event proposed a new trait method instead. On a single event versus one per case, Antonio: one event is fine only with a `kind` field, so a listener can skip what it does not need.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Client side exists: ChromeCtx::on (heca/src/providers/mod.rs:391) over app.on; names in heca/src/chrome/state/events.rs:235. Server side done in P111(F012)/T568: ServiceRegistration::on (heca/src/entry/service/mod.rs), ServerEvent/SessionEvent (heca/src/entry/service/sessions.rs), raised only by ServerLoop::announce_session (heca/src/server/run/mod.rs), also StreamEvent::SessionChanged (heca/src/server/events.rs). `folder_changed` dropped from the kinds: no command changes a session's folder today; add it with the command that does. Plugins: F003/T79 (event bus bridge to WASM) must expose exactly this line. Highlighted as "⭐ THE EVENTS" in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md § 0, docs/plugins.md and docs/extending-heca.md (T568).

acceptedDecisions.title: The window's widget tree is laid out every frame; skipping layout when nothing changed is not done
acceptedDecisions.decision: heca-grid-ui keeps laying out the whole window tree on every frame (heca/src/chrome/window/scene/mod.rs paint_chrome_root → LayoutEngine::compute). A "layout only when something asked" pass was studied in P110(F010)/T572 (point D) and dropped with Antonio on 2026-11-19.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Measured with macOS `sample` under a heavy load: layout is ~6% of the window's main thread, and the window is GPU-bound (most time waits in nextDrawable), so the gain is small. Skipping safely needs every layout-affecting change to announce itself. Signals read while a widget is measured can be tracked once in the engine (layout/build.rs remeasure/taffy_style/measure_text), but many changes bypass signals: ~210 direct assignments to style.layout in heca-grid-ui (+13 in heca), ~90 places that push/remove/replace children, and Label text changes do not mark needs_layout today (layout every frame is what keeps them right). Two ways were weighed: make each of those places announce the change (a rule every author must remember — rejected), or compare every widget's style and measure inputs with the previous frame (generic, but costs a large part of the layout itself, leaving perhaps half of the 6%). Neither is worth the risk of stale text and sizes that tests cannot see. heca-pro asked nothing about it (checked the planner).
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: If it is ever revisited: make Base's needs_layout start true for a new widget, track signal reads around the measure block in layout/build.rs, and compare style.layout + child count + measure_text/intrinsic_size per node for everything else; measure the compare walk against LayoutEngine::compute before switching. Layout spikes of ~19 ms come from full chrome rebuilds, which need a layout anyway.
